content:
**Pump and dump (P&D) detection in crypto** combines price/volume spikes, order flow analysis, fakeout identification, and machine learning techniques like meta-labeling for robust signal filtering. These schemes involve coordinated buying to inflate prices (pump), followed by selling into retail demand (dump), often in low-liquidity tokens. [[1]](https://alphaarchitect.com/a-new-wolf-in-town-pump-and-dump-manipulation-in-cryptocurrency-markets/) [[2]](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40163-018-0093-5)

Typical P&D anatomy: gradual pre-pump accumulation, sharp price/volume surge (often 20-65%+ with 10x+ volume), peak, then rapid reversal. Detection relies on anomaly thresholds relative to recent history (e.g., EWMA or moving averages). [[3]](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.08692v1) [[2]](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40163-018-0093-5)

### Key Features for Detection (Pre-Entry and Order Flow)
Effective models use time-series features from price, volume, and order flow. Common ones include:

- **Price-based**: % change from recent MA, std dev of price, momentum (e.g., returns over short windows), breakouts vs. exhaustion (failure to hold new highs/lows). [[4]](https://massimolamorgia.com/assets/pdf/Pump_Dump__ICCCN__2020.pdf)
- **Volume-based**: Sudden spikes (e.g., >5-10x average), Avg/Std of volumes or "rush orders," volume profile (high-volume nodes as support/resistance). Exhaustion shows climactic volume followed by decline. [[3]](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.08692v1) [[5]](https://bookmap.com/blog/volume-profile-order-flow-tools-for-deep-market-insight)
- **Order Flow**: Buy/sell imbalance (e.g., cumulative volume delta - CVD), proportion of buy orders, aggressive buyer/seller pressure, order book depth/imbalance. Tools like footprint/cluster charts or DOM reveal absorption or exhaustion. [[6]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rqu-AoD9BUo) [[7]](https://optimusfutures.com/blog/order-flow-analysis/)
- **Other**: Market cap/liquidity (low-cap coins more vulnerable), social/Telegram signals (for coordinated pumps), time-of-day encodings (sin/cos), volatility measures. [[8]](https://tesi.luiss.it/39106/1/756851_CUNIATO_GUGLIELMO.pdf)

**Pump exhaustion and fake breakouts** are critical for entries. Real breakouts show sustained volume and follow-through; fakes show wicks, weak volume, quick reversals (e.g., swing failure patterns - SFP), or liquidity grabs (stop hunts). Exhaustion: high volume with divergence (price makes higher high but momentum/volume fades). [[9]](https://www.quantvps.com/blog/swing-failure-pattern-strategy?srsltid=AfmBOoohaIzNA7rtwmQb4Vr973-giO1vwqV2GYP_bB6BUyHIgxsF-f1j) [[10]](https://chartscout.io/how-to-spot-fake-breakouts-crypto)

Pre-entry checks: Confirm volume expansion on genuine moves; avoid low-volume spikes. Use multi-timeframe confirmation and wait for retests or closes beyond levels.

### Entry Strategy with Risk Management
- **Long pump entry** (risky, often front-run): Early detection via order flow surge or Telegram signals, but high slippage risk in illiquid pairs. Better: Fade exhaustion on dumps or trade post-pump mean-reversion if signals align. [[11]](https://www.colibritrader.com/pump-and-dump-guide/)
- **Fake breakout fade**: Enter opposite the fake move on confirmation (e.g., candle close back inside range + volume drop). Tight stops above the fake high. [[12]](https://www.cointracker.io/learn/false-breakout-in-trading)
- **Slippage risk**: Model via market impact (trade size vs. expected volume/volatility/spreads). Use execution alphas or limit orders; smaller sizes in low-liquidity. Crypto's thin books amplify this—forecast intraday conditions. [[13]](https://www.talos.com/insights/execution-alphas-in-crypto-markets-predicting-volume-volatility-and-spreads-to-reduce-slippage)

Always size small, use stops, and avoid chasing.

### Meta-Labeling for Signal Filtering
**Meta-labeling** (from Marcos Lopez de Prado) layers ML on a primary strategy. Primary model generates signals (e.g., breakout or P&D anomaly detector). Secondary ML model predicts if the trade will be profitable (meta-label: 1 = win, 0 = loss), filtering false positives. [[14]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZCFmZFBtqsQ) [[15]](https://hudsonthames.org/meta-labeling-a-toy-example/)

**How it works**:
1. Primary: Rule-based (e.g., price/volume thresholds) or ML for P&D detection.
2. Labels: Triple-barrier (profit target, stop-loss, time horizon) or continuous trend for each signal.
3. Features: Same as primary + regime (volatility, order flow strength), performance diagnostics.
4. Train secondary classifier (e.g., Random Forest, XGBoost) to output probability → size or skip.

This improves Sharpe, reduces drawdowns by avoiding weak setups (e.g., low-volume fakeouts). Applied successfully to Bollinger Bands or trend strategies in crypto. [[16]](https://medium.com/@liangnguyen612/meta-labeling-in-cryptocurrencies-market-95f761410fac)

### Time Series Validation and Model Building
Financial time series are non-stationary—use **purged cross-validation** (e.g., embargo periods) or walk-forward optimization to avoid leakage. Avoid simple random splits. [[17]](https://mlfinpy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Labelling.html)

- **Labeling**: Triple-barrier or continuous trend (tracks sustained moves beyond fixed horizons). [[18]](https://www.mdpi.com/1099-4300/22/10/1162)
- **Models**: Unsupervised (EWMA + thresholds for anomalies), supervised (RF, XGBoost on features), deep learning (LSTM/Transformers for sequences). Ensemble methods excel with imbalanced data (SMOTE). [[3]](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.08692v1) [[19]](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373529266_Detecting_Pump-and-Dumps_with_Crypto-Assets_Dealing_with_Imbalanced_Datasets_and_Insiders'_Anticipated_Purchases)
- **Validation**: Expanding window, time-based splits; metrics like F1 (for early detection), precision-recall for rare events.

Real-time pipelines monitor Telegram + high-frequency order book/trades (e.g., 5-30s chunks, 30min-7h windows). [[20]](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18848v1)

### Practical Tips and Caveats
- **Data**: Exchanges like Poloniex, Binance; combine with on-chain/social. [[3]](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.08692v1)
- **Challenges**: Many "pumps" are organic; low-liquidity noise; regulatory gray areas. Models achieve high recall but need human oversight.
- **Tools**: Volume profile, order flow platforms (Bookmap, etc.), ML libs (scikit-learn, mlfinlab for meta-labeling).

This framework—features from price/volume/order flow, anomaly/fakeout detection, meta-labeling for filtering, and rigorous time-series validation—provides a solid base for building or improving a P&D-aware trading system. Start with backtesting on historical pumps, then paper trade. Markets evolve, so retrain regularly.

1 INTRODUCTION P UMP and dump schemes are the bane of any ambitious crypotrader’s existence. Pump and dump refers to the process of a bad actor artiﬁcially raising the price (the pump) and subsequent selling to make a large proﬁt (dump). While traditional stock markets have legal safeguards that prohibit pump and dump schemes, the wild west of crypto has no such assurances, and are far more common in this domain.
Successfully detecting pump and dump schemes will help prevent trading losses during the ”dump” phase of the cycle. Traders also stand to make a lot of money from the pump phase of the cycle, in which market book activity manipulates traders into believing that the price of an asset (or cryptocurrency in this case) is higher than it should be. [...] This research presented the broad framework for our own application as its principles are generalizable to any liquid market. We too used level 2 data to label our dataset but trained and evaluated our models with level 1 data.
3 DATASET AND FEATURES After creating API keys for Poloniex, a widely used crypto exchange, we built infrastructure to request, ﬁlter, and compress publicly available order data between USD and a variety of other crypto-currencies: ’ETH’,’XMR’, ’DASH’, ’XRP’, and ’LTC’.
Poloniex provides a JSON of up to 50,000 orders for a given crypto-pair between two unix timestamps. Initially, we manually identiﬁed obvious pump and dumps and then called our scraping function to fetch relevant order data. [...] 4 METHODS The difﬁculty of solving our problem is that we have no access to cancel order data from the API offered by the exchange we monitor, Poloniex. Instead, we need to ﬁnd a way to detect artiﬁcial pumps using an asset’s order book, which is a public ally available set of buy and sell orders with transaction volumes. Left with just this order book as our feature space, we have massive amounts of unstructured data that must somehow ﬁgure out how to surmise whether anomalous price spikes are occurring without direct access to the smoking gun cancel order data.

sources.description: Abstract: Detecting pump-and-dump schemes involving cryptoassets with high-frequency data is challenging due to imbalanced datasets and the early occurrence of unusual trading volumes. To address these issues, we propose constructing synthetic balanced datasets using resampling methods and flagging a pump-and-dump from the moment of public announcement up to 60 min beforehand. We validated our proposals using data from Pumpolymp and the CryptoCurrency eXchange Trading Library to identify 351 pump signals relative to the Binance crypto exchange in 2021 and 2022. We found that the most effective approach was using the original imbalanced dataset with pump-and-dumps flagged 60 min in advance, together with a random forest model with data segmented into 30-s chunks and regressors computed

This section contains the features we found to be most effective for the classification of coins into pumpable and non-pumpable. Initially, we calculated 27 features from the OHLCV (open, high, low, close, volume), market capitalization, and social time series data, which we collected for a sample of 1,714 coins (643 pumped coins and a random sample of 1,071 non-pump coins). Key metrics include order book pressure, average order size, order imbalance ratio, market order impact, volume-weighted average price (VWAP), high-low spread, and trade count.
